# Review of SEEN-109, attempt 3, from the seen-reviewer subagent

Spawned on opus with the task text of triage record 35 and nothing else. It read
the ticket, all thirty-five records, the nineteen files of the focus set, the
calibration report, `harness/journal.py`, `harness/paths.py`,
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `CLAUDE.md`. `reviewer_session` is null for the
reason note 17 gives.

Verdict: **return**, on F1 and F2.

It confirmed both earlier returns as properly answered: no character-stripping
path comparison remains anywhere in `harness/`, every comparison in
`calibration.py` goes through `normalise`, a returning round's findings are
read, going live names the record its decision is in, and `counted_from` matches
commit ea499b1 to the second. It accepted note 28's disowning of slice 1's
second RED as the honest answer and did not re-raise it.

## The findings

**F1, medium, `harness/cli.py:747`.** A returning round's findings reach the
window only if the session remembers `--findings`, and nothing that affects the
verdict notices when it did not. The omission writes an unattributable row, and
the rule counts unattributable neither way, so the ticket still reads clean and
ten such tickets state go-live on a window that hid exactly the escape kind it
measures.

**F2, medium, `harness/calibration.py:400`.** Every printed go-live instruction
still says one line while the implementation demands two. A founder who follows
the report sets `triage_shadow` to false, commits, and turns CI red on every
branch while the go-live the report authorised does nothing. The same
instruction is in `thresholds.toml`'s `triage_rule`, which the report prints
verbatim, in `report.py`, and in `skill.md`, where it contradicts its own
paragraph nineteen lines later.

**F3, low, `harness/calibration.py:317`.** A ticket whose receipt was voided by
`harness reopen` still counts as delivered, so a ticket being worked can join
the window and a verdict can be taken on a review round that has not happened.

**F4, low, `harness/calibration.py:476`.** `verdict_routes` reports a window of
every route-carrying ticket while its rates come from the last ten, so a founder
auditing the decision recomputes over a list the verdict was not taken on.

**F5, low, `harness/tests/test_calibration.py:621`.** No test distinguishes
charging a repeated finding to the earliest round's triage from charging it to
the latest: the fixture plants the same exclusions in both triages, so keeping
the last occurrence instead of the first leaves the suite green.

**F6, low, `harness/calibration.py:34`.** `journals` reads every ticket's
journal unguarded from inside the triage and from doctor, where the read beside
it is guarded. A stray file in one journal would refuse the review stage of
every other ticket.

**F7, low, the ticket file.** Criterion 1 keeps wording the ticket deliberately
did not meet, without the `(as amended)` marker this repository uses for exactly
that, so a ticked box would be false on its face.

**F8, low, `docs/harness/workflow.md:86`.** A sentence in the rewritten
paragraph begins in lower case.

## The deterministic checks it was handed

`red_before_green` verified against the cited outputs for both slices and both
later attempts, line for line. `tests_added` passes but for F5.
`acceptance_entries` passes. `slice_files` it passed, naming all three files
outside the slice plan and noting that `harness/doctor.py` is described in the
Outcome but not named there as one of them. `pull_request` stayed unavailable.
It checked the ground rules over the whole diff and found the only dash inside
repowise's quoted output in record 2.

## What the shadow window will read from this round

The triage would have excluded 12 of 19 files, 53.18 per cent. No finding is at
high or blocking severity, so there is no escape of either kind and nothing
unattributable. The round reads clean, and the ticket is excluded from the
window by name in any case.
